method: Full text PDF read (abstract, results, limitations).

claims.claim: A review of 15 studies found each additional weekly set was associated with slightly more muscle growth.
claims.source_title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis
claims.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
claims.study_type: Systematic review and meta-analysis (15 studies, 34 treatment groups)
claims.finding: Graded dose-response; each additional weekly set associated with ES +0.023 (about +0.37% gain).

claims.claim: On average, 10+ weekly sets per muscle showed larger gains than fewer than 5 (hedged: 'في المتوسط').
claims.finding: Mean ES 0.307 (<5 sets, ~5.4%), 0.378 (5-9, ~6.6%), 0.520 (10+, ~9.8%); category comparison was a trend (P = 0.074) and sensitive to one study, hence the hedge.

claims.claim: The upper limit is unknown and studies on advanced trainees are few.
claims.finding: Authors: too little data above about 12 weekly sets; 'it remains unclear as to where the upper threshold lies'; only two studies in resistance-trained people.

limitations: Recovery-based progression in the takeaway is practical guidance, not a study finding.
